newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: ACPC may discuss loosening export limits in Copan.
newsitem.headline: ACPC may discuss loosening export limits in Copan.

text.p: Costa Rican coffee sources said Tuesday there is a possibility of a petition to loosen export limits at a regional meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) next week.
The sources, who requested anonimity, said there could be a motion in Honduras to make limits more flexible. The sources did not name which nation might put forward the proposal.

Central American ACPC members meet Feb 17-18 at the Mayan ruins of Copan alongside regional partners Ecuador and Venezuela. Colombia has also been invited. Such regional ACPC meetings do not have the power to make definitive decisions.
"There is interest in liberating certain quantities in order to remove market pressures," said one source.
The coffee sources argued that with world prices rising the continuation of ACPC pressures to limit supply would be tantamount to "a stance of exaggerated ambition."
Another source said; "To continue holding back coffee is gluttony."

The sources said it would be preferable to hold prices in a firm and steady range between $120.00 to $135.00 per 100-lb quintal rather than to have to be at the whim of wild market price fluctuations.

Ricardo Seevers, vice chairman of the Costa Rican Coffee Institute, refused to confirm or deny the versions that there could be a motion to loosen export limits of ACPC members, saying a fixed agenda had not been established.
"Alongside looking at the market movements in the last weeks, we will be revising the results of the export limit scheme in place since July 1, 1996," Seevers said.

Honduran coffee officials said earlier Tuesday the Copan meeting is a routine regional gathering on the back of the recent full ACPC meeting in Rio de Janeiro, where the council tweaked exports limits a little tighter to cut supplies.
